premise: After my husband’s death, I used his $85,000 rare‑coin collection as seed capital to open a dealership with my stepson on a signed 49% partnership; when he sold a 1913 Liberty Head nickel for $700,000, he forged my release, kept the cash, and locked me out. I dug up an authenticated photo of my late husband with the coin’s receipt, sued my stepson for conversion, and was awarded $350,000 plus the shop’s inventory—I rebranded as ‘Proof of Betrayal Numismatics,’ and he now works as a coin polisher while a looped video of his deposition plays on the sales counter and his hourly wage is garnished.
